planting.note: Pot rooted cuttings in spring in a well-drained aroid mix; grow trailing from a shelf or basket, or train vertically up a pole for larger, more dramatic foliage.

directions: Lemon Top is a pothos selection whose new heart-shaped leaves emerge a bright lemon-yellow to lime-green before gradually deepening to green with age, giving the plant a two-toned, sunlit look. It tolerates low indoor light but holds its brightest coloring and most vigorous growth in medium to bright indirect light, including some gentle morning sun. Let the top couple of inches of potting mix dry before rewatering, and train it up a pole or across a mantle for a bolder display as the leaves enlarge.

planting.note: Pot rooted cuttings in spring in a well-drained aroid mix; situate within a few feet of an east- or west-facing window for best color, or grow farther back in lower light with slower growth.

directions: Neon Joy produces small, glowing lime-green leaves irregularly edged in medium green, a compact-leaved counterpart to larger-leaved pothos cultivars. It tolerates low light but colors up and grows fastest in medium to bright indirect light, and it can climb more than ten feet if left unpruned or stay tidy as a trailing tabletop plant with regular trimming. Allow roughly the top half of the potting mix to dry between waterings, since it dislikes staying constantly wet.

planting.note: Pot rooted cuttings in spring in chunky, well-drained aroid mix; provide a moss pole or trellis so the vine can climb, since leaves enlarge dramatically with vertical support.

directions: Also sold under the nickname Silver Splash, this Scindapsus selection carries teardrop-shaped dark green leaves heavily mottled with silver and olive, giving a sparkly look in bright conditions. It grows well under medium to bright artificial or natural light and does not need direct sun to thrive, though it performs best when given a support to climb rather than left to trail, where it can otherwise send out bare, leafless runners. Let the top couple of inches of mix dry between waterings and avoid overwatering, which it tolerates poorly.

planting.note: Pot rooted divisions or cuttings in spring in a well-drained, humus-rich aroid mix; display at eye level as a tabletop specimen since it grows medium to slow and won't quickly outgrow its spot.

directions: Rhodospatha Rojo is a lesser-known aroid relative of Monstera and Philodendron grown for its glossy deep-green foliage flushed with purple above and a striking chocolatey-red color beneath each leaf. It survives a wide range of indoor light levels and does well under artificial lighting, with a spot a few feet from an east- or west-facing window giving the most consistent growth. It can tolerate occasional drying out but looks best with steady moisture, and its medium-to-slow growth rate makes it a manageable specimen for smaller indoor spaces.

planting.note: Pot rooted cuttings with at least one node in spring in a chunky, well-drained aroid mix; give a moss pole or trellis to climb so fenestrations develop as the plant matures.

directions: This variegated form of Monstera lechleriana carries medium-green leaves splashed and streaked with creamy white, making it a sought-after variegated counterpart to the solid-green species. It survives in low light but fills out fuller and holds more variegation in medium to bright indirect light, and like other lechleriana selections it can climb more than six feet with good support, developing fenestrations more slowly than Monstera adansonii. Allow the top couple of inches of potting mix to dry between waterings and avoid letting it sit wet, since overwatering is its main vulnerability.

planting.note: Plant container stock in spring or fall in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil mulched to protect its shallow roots; blooms on old wood, so prune only right after flowering.

directions: Fairytrail Green is a cascading mophead hydrangea that sets a bloom at nearly every leaf node along its gracefully arching stems, creating a fountain-like curtain of cool lime-green flowers that do not shift with soil pH the way typical mopheads do. Give it part shade with roughly four to six hours of sun, since more exposure scorches its foliage and weakens stems, and mulch well since its shallow roots dry out quickly. Its loose, trailing habit suits large containers, hanging baskets, or draping over a retaining wall in a shaded border.

planting.note: Plant container stock in spring or fall in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil mulched to protect its shallow roots; blooms on old wood, so prune only right after flowering.

directions: Fairytrail White (USPP 35,989) shares the same every-node-blooms trailing habit as its Fairytrail Green sibling, lining its graceful arching stems with white mophead flowers so densely that each node appears topped with its own bloom. Grow it in part shade with about four to six hours of sun, mulching to conserve moisture for its shallow root system, and prune only immediately after flowering since buds form on old wood. Its cascading, spiller-type form works well draping from hanging baskets or over a shaded wall or container edge.
